# Test Video 2 — consolidated ground-truth-driven evaluation and improvement

Both Test2 arms are genuine complete fresh pipeline runs. Test1's new regression reuses immutable perception and is **not fresh neural inference**. Original Part2 files and historical benchmarks remain separate and unchanged; this is a per-video result, not a ten-video aggregate.

Supplied human-origin coarse labels, generated support predictions and source-reviewed diagnostic evidence are distinguished below. Unavailable accuracy is never converted to zero. Counts, execution success and regression tests do not establish physical sporting correctness. Displayed numbers use up to10 significant digits; sibling JSON and linked original metrics preserve full numeric precision.

## Outcome and evidence scope

| Fresh Test2 arm | TP | FP | FN | Precision | Recall | F1 | Mean IoU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 68 | 7 | 5 | 0.9066666667 | 0.9315068493 | 0.9189189189 | 0.8481346537 |
| Fresh post-fix | 68 | 7 | 5 | 0.9066666667 | 0.9315068493 | 0.9189189189 | 0.8493108146 |

The implemented change is **racket_anatomical_alias_abstention_v1**: retain raw equipment geometry, but withhold its semantic racket cue when it aliases fresh facial landmarks. It does not retrain models, establish racket/contact ground truth, resolve torso/background aliases or manufacture identities, points or winners.

## Complete three-reference before/after matrix and every original row

Matching is unchanged: IoU≥0.5 maximum cardinality, then total IoU with the existing boundary-distance tie term. IoU/boundary/duration statistics condition on matched pairs; TP/FP/FN retain every missed and extra interval.

## Source-bound semantic side effects and contact-NMS risk

The following independent event review concerns controlled semantic replays; any Test2 cached-replay reporting failure remains separate from the completed fresh Test2 arm above.
## Practical semantic effects of the anatomical-alias admission fix

This review independently compares original live events with the changed-engine
replays on **unchanged recorded perception**. These are semantic regressions,
not fresh neural inference or independent physical accuracy evaluation. Original
events, raw observations, videos, annotations and previous reports are unchanged.

Test1 and Test2 fixed-perception reviews are complete below. Test2 uses the
recovered guarded completion receipt after safe report-only recovery; the child
replay was not rerun. Its missing schedule-feedback witness at frontier119
remains explicit uncertainty. The separate fresh post-fix Test2 neural run is
needed before claiming full-pipeline preservation.

### Test1: headline effects

| Output | Before | Changed-engine replay | Meaning |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Live contact events | 446 | 445 | Net count alone hides temporal anchor changes. |
| Live stroke events | 446 | 445 | Same changed anchors as contacts. |
| Exact old anchors absent | — | 14 | Thirteen have nearby replacement candidates. |
| New exact anchors | — | 13 | Paired diagnostically as possible shifts, not new physical GT. |
| Nearby temporal shift pairs | — | 13 | Changes range−3 to+6frames; largest absolute shift0.2s. |
| Unpaired removed anchor | — | 15801/526.700s | Its own support is unchanged; neighborhood competition explains disappearance. |
| New anatomical ambiguity events | 0 | 2047 | Raw candidate retained; specific equipment cue withheld. |
| Rally intervals | 36 | 36 | All six saved reference metric sets are identical. |
| Canonical accepted point events | 0 | 0 | No winner/score accuracy improvement established. |
| Live highlight events | 3 | 4 | Heuristic selection changed despite identical rally boundaries. |

The controlling regression also verifies287 nonterminal perception-driver
frontiers unchanged. This supports fixed-perception isolation. It does not make
the changed contact/classification/attribution outputs independently correct.

Independent evidence: [compact event diff](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/evaluation/ground_truth_validation/test_02/fixes/semantic_effect_evidence/test_01/event_diff.json),
[complete changed events](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/evaluation/ground_truth_validation/test_02/fixes/semantic_effect_evidence/test_01/complete_changed_event_evidence.json).
Matching pairs absent old/new contact anchors within15frames/0.5s and the same
containing rally interval, maximizing cardinality then minimizing frame distance.
All observed pairs here are within6frames. This associates nearby estimates;
it does not certify that two estimates describe the same physical impact.

### Test1: same-anchor classification and provisional actor changes

At2404/80.133333s, unknown becomes `net_shot`; the provisional hitter changes from
unresolved to visual track1. The contact's physical status changes from
insufficient to ambiguous. The source-bound ambiguity event withholds track1's
head-like equipment candidate at513.967,359.930: it encloses all five facial
landmarks of **the other visible person, track0**. This is a real cross-person
anatomical alias, not just an own-head case. Another surviving contour is still
only a raw estimate. The changed proximity anchor can alter attribution without
establishing the true hitter or stroke.

At8172/272.400s, `drop` becomes `push` and the provisional hitter changes from
track0 to track1. Both visible head ellipses are withheld from specific racket
evidence. The image shows live rally action; no supplied independent per-contact
label resolves the class or hitter. See
[raw versus semantic overlay](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/evaluation/ground_truth_validation/test_02/fixes/semantic_effect_evidence/test_01/frame_08172_raw_vs_semantic.png).

At12874/429.133333s, the predicted label stays `push`, but the provisional hitter
changes from track2 to track1 and the internal physical status changes from
ambiguous to probable. The near head ellipse is withheld while a far/background
candidate remains. This demonstrates that removing one misleading cue can
**increase** a downstream heuristic assessment by changing its selected actor.
It is not a verified physical contact or calibrated correctness probability.

The other same-anchor provisional track switches occur at7414(0→1),7730(2→1),
8222(0→1),14626(0→1). These are visual tracker episodes, not named athletes.
No canonical player/team identity or accepted point was created.

Scores, class labels and provisional attribution remain model/rule outputs.

### Test1: exact removed-anchor mechanism

The removed15801/526.700s candidate had no racket observation on that frame.
Its original physical-impact assessment was insufficient because no current
detector-matched player was recorded. Neither fact proves there was no physical
impact. The source image shows live action and a far player's extended racket
near the predicted shuttle region:
[frame15801](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/evaluation/ground_truth_validation/test_02/fixes/semantic_effect_evidence/test_01/frame_15801_raw_vs_semantic.png).

A bounded CPU score/NMS probe uses the exact frozen person/pose observations and
the original processed shuttle trace over15755–15899. It reproduces the original
contact-eligible peaks15801,15809,15843 and the new peaks15809,15843, including
their exact stored confidence values. It performs no neural inference.

| Frame | Original support | Admission-policy support | Explanation |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 15801 | 0.4502698471 | 0.4502698471 | Candidate's own score is unchanged. |
| 15806 | 0.2841034673 | 0.4610637889 | Replacing anatomical racket anchors with wrists changes proximity0.3682→0.5941; score crosses unchanged0.35threshold. |
| 15808 | 0.7783656885 | 0.8351438998 | Proximity changes0.3789→0.4866. |
| 15809 | 0.9373433904 | 0.9373433904 | Stronger retained neighboring peak is unchanged. |

The existing local-maximum suppression radius is6frames/0.2s. New15806
suppresses15801, but15808 and15809 in turn suppress15806. Thus15801 disappears
through a neighborhood competition cascade even though the competing15806 is
not ultimately retained. This is the behavior of the existing local-maximum
rule, not evidence that NMS is defective. No NMS rule or threshold was changed.

[Exact bounded score/NMS evidence](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/evaluation/ground_truth_validation/test_02/fixes/semantic_effect_evidence/test_01/temporal_competition_v2.json),
[executed CPU probe](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/evaluation/ground_truth_validation/test_02/fixes/semantic_effect_evidence/test_01/executed_temporal_probe.py),
[probe output](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/evaluation/ground_truth_validation/test_02/fixes/semantic_effect_evidence/test_01/temporal_probe_v2.log).

The practical implication is important: a conservative equipment admission rule
can still remove or shift a potentially real contact through downstream peak
selection. Without independently reviewed impact times, this cannot be called
false-contact removal or a recall improvement. The preserved source and raw
observations allow later adjudication.

### Test1: highlights and unchanged rally metrics

Live highlight events increase3→4. The additional selected interval is
14430–15171, heuristic score4.2, with length3.0 and predicted shot-variety1.2
contributions. This is distinct from the downstream exporter's fixed top-k
highlight list. No highlight relevance labels certify that the added selection
is better.

All six interval-reference metric sets remain unchanged, so Test1 rally timing
regression is preserved under this fixed-perception comparison. That statement
does not imply unchanged contacts, strokes, provisional hitters or highlights.

### Limits and required next evidence

- Anatomical ambiguity is a narrow semantic-admission safeguard. Background and
  torso ellipses remain unresolved; surviving candidates are not certified rackets.
- The source overlays use the exact original neural-analysis proxy and raw
  cached predictions. They show the same pixels before/after; the distinction
  comes from recorded admission events, not regenerated detections.
- Contact timing, hitter identity and class accuracy require reviewed per-impact
  labels; filled shuttle trajectories and two generated player slots cannot
  supply that truth.
- Test2 report recovery is complete, but its one unobserved schedule frontier
  remains unresolved in these recorded observations. A fresh full Test2 pipeline
  run is separate from these semantic replays and supplies current end-to-end
  evidence only after its own completed guards and evaluation.
- No additional pipeline fix, NMS adjustment, threshold tuning or production
  helper change was made by this review.


### Test2: scope, recovered completion and practical counts

The completed regression consumes all **29,296 canonical frames at30fps** on the
exact Test2 source. Recovery preserved the initial failure log and old helper,
validated the already-completed child artifacts, and regenerated reporting only.
[Recovered completion](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/ground-truth-validation-artifacts-20261110/test_02/test2_semantic_regression_v1/completion.json),
[saved full reference matrices](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/ground-truth-validation-artifacts-20261110/test_02/test2_semantic_regression_v1/semantic_regression_metrics.json).
It did not repeat replay or neural inference. Of488 requested nonterminal
schedule frontiers,487 are observed and agree; **frontier119 is unknown** because
the retained original trace resets from95 to179 around a format change. There
is no claim that the unobserved scheduling input matches. Fresh Test2 inference
is required for full end-to-end preservation.

The diagnostic matcher pairs absent/new anchors within15frames/0.5s and the same
chronological containing rally ordinal, maximizing cardinality then minimizing
absolute displacement. It first requires equal rally populations and overlap
IoU≥0.5 for every same-ordinal interval. Every observed pair moves just1frame.
The earlier preserved Test2 review required identical boundary tuples; that
prevented four valid *diagnostic* associations when boundaries changed. Final
v2 uses ordinal context; neither association proves physical event identity.
The original v1 evidence remains preserved and is not the final pairing count.

### Review provenance and interpretation

- Test1 source SHA256: `877c6d39d34ccfb302865ed44f7e08949b0f72be2833f71777066f837e6b8bd6`.
- Test2 source SHA256: `4d687b4240fd501fb723c50588ecd095b9d9863299108c9d43b77c9587ba3c0a`.
- Applied code, before/after source hashes and regressions are recorded in
  [applied fix receipt](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/evaluation/ground_truth_validation/test_02/fixes/applied_fix_receipt.json). This review changes none of it.
- Completed semantic input/event/cache/proxy hashes and exact executed diagnostic
  helper are preserved in each evidence directory. Test2 final pairing uses
  `test_02_v2`; earlier `test_02` artifacts are retained for provenance.
- Review confirms a narrow correction in the evidence contract: equipment that
  overlaps reliable facial evidence is retained raw and explicitly withheld from
  semantic equipment use. It does not validate every abstention or detect the
  true racket. Real overhead rackets can overlap faces, and background contours
  remain unresolved.
- Both videos exhibit practical downstream effects beyond racket counts:
  temporal peak changes, provisional hitter selection, class abstention or new
  labels, and highlights. Test2 also changes six rally boundaries. The exact
  Test1 score/NMS probe explains one cascade; other changed contacts are not
  claimed to share that exact mechanism without a separate local probe.
- No contact/racket/stroke/identity accuracy gain is claimed. All original
  videos, annotations, prediction baselines and raw caches remain unmodified.
  No new pipeline fix, threshold tuning or production/helper edit was made by
  this review. The separate fresh Test2 run must pass its own completion and
  metric guards before it can support a fresh before/after conclusion.

## Ranked diagnosis and remaining improvement priorities

1. **Confirmed correctness repair, evaluated above:** anatomical ellipse aliases previously entered semantic racket evidence. The narrow admission repair withholds facial aliases while preserving raw geometry. Neither cache execution nor the generated filled-ball files establish its physical precision/recall.
2. **Confirmed baseline perception/continuity limitations:** background-official admission at6492 and propagated-box failures at355/25521 survive favorable aggregate player-point agreement. Their first incorrect detector/tracker/admission update remains unresolved; no fitted distance cutoff was introduced. The baseline also missed actual source/player-layout edit11346; its G69 split follows a22-frame raw-decoder gap, end publication and reacquisition beyond the existing merge window. These mechanisms are source/cache/trace-bound; neither a blanket scene reset nor a merge-threshold change has demonstrated safe improvement. Inspect the negative walking/retrieval controls before changing temporal policy.
3. **Confirmed product coverage limits:** verified athlete identity, contact attribution, winners and accepted scoring remain dependent on missing roster/identity/outcome evidence. Unknowns and empty named-player analytics/heatmaps must remain visible. Torso/background racket aliases and ambiguous shuttle branches remain outside the narrow facial policy.
4. **Annotation ambiguity rather than established code defects:** anonymous player slots are not permanent athletes; historical scoreboard columns differ from current-game scores; coarse boundaries can include preparation/retrieval. Generated winners and filled shuttle positions are diagnostic agreement targets. Duplicate ball files and out-of-canvas positions must not increase the independent sample population.
5. **Rejected alternatives:** forcing full-corner OCR did not resolve the actual readout gap and removed a correct9/12 countercontrol. Lowering short-rally duration/evidence gates would admit a walking control. No Test2-fitted threshold, brand blacklist, synthesized track or guessed winner was adopted.

Priorities above describe observed failure mechanisms and missing evidence; proposed future changes require independent labels, source review, preserved before/after metrics and Test1 regression checks. Detailed baseline cases and the separate fresh post-fix measurements follow.

### Schemas and conventions, verified from content and producers

#### Coarse outcome table

`start_time,end_time` are whole-second `MM:SS` strings; all 75 spans are parseable, positive and ordered without adjacent overlap. They are coarse sporting intervals, not exact one-frame boundaries. `win_point_player` is symbolic `Player A` or `Player B` (27 A, 48 B). `win_reason` has 32 `Opponent Out of Bounds`, 22 `Winner Shot`, and 21 `Opponent Hit the Net`; `lose_reason` has the complementary three strings. `ball_types` has **15 distinct values** and one entry per rally: Lift Shot, Smash, Lob, Net Shot, Drive Defense, Drive, Clear, Net Kill, Cross Net Shot, Push Shot, Long Serve, Slice, Block, Stick Smash and Defensive Slice. It is not an exhaustive contact sequence or a direct replacement for the current stroke taxonomy. `roundscore_A,roundscore_B` parse as integer-valued scores.

Legacy documentation [`legacy/pipeline/docs/10_evaluation.md`](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/legacy/pipeline/docs/10_evaluation.md) identifies the eight primary `<match>.csv` tables as hand-labelled, separately from generated support files. This establishes documented origin, not certification that every row is correct or a held-out prospective test. Retain the originals and record any new reviewed interpretation separately.

The documented legacy reason adapter is:

| Supplied coarse label | Legacy class | Restriction |
|---|---|---|
| Opponent Out of Bounds | out_of_bounds | Outcome reason, not a physical landing coordinate label |
| Opponent Hit the Net | hits_net | Outcome reason, not an exhaustive racket/contact sequence |
| Winner Shot / Opponent Failed to Return | wins_by_landing | Legacy taxonomy mapping; does not certify a precise landing event |

The legacy winner predictor declares `Player A=far`, `Player B=near` in [`win_predictor/README.md`](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/legacy/pipeline/win_predictor/README.md), and maps a near fault to A and a far fault to B in `predict.py`. **That producer convention does not independently prove that the primary human-origin A/B labels follow persistent athletes, camera sides or scoreboard rows throughout this edited multi-game clip.** Bind source players, changes of ends, game resets and scoreboard rows before named-identity or score accuracy claims. Current unknown identities must remain unknown.

#### Generated rally and outcome tables

Rally columns: `Start_Frame,End_Frame` are integer indices; `Start_Time_sec,End_Time_sec,Duration_sec` are floating-point seconds; `Start_Time,End_Time` are coarse display strings. All 73 exact time pairs equal frame indices divided by 30 within 1e-6; all durations equal end minus start. Use exact frame/seconds fields for comparisons; do not reparse the truncated display strings as exact times or add an undocumented inclusive-end frame. The generating code `legacy/pipeline/analysis/detect_rallies.py` writes the same schema after detection, merging and lookback.

Winner columns: `rally_idx` is zero based; `start_frame,end_frame` identify the interval; `start_time,end_time` are display strings; `winner,loser` are symbolic labels; `win_reason,reason_src,fault_side,fault_src,cnn_class` are generated categorical outputs; `cnn_conf,cnn_oob,cnn_hn,cnn_wbl` are model scores; `score_Player A,score_Player B` are reconstructed cumulative points. Their presence does not make those scores calibrated probabilities or independently reviewed results.

All **73 of 73** winner frame pairs equal the corresponding rally rows. Generated winners are 29 A and 44 B, with final running score **29–44**; `predict.py` increments from predicted winners without a game-aware GT ledger. These values must not be compared blindly with primary scores or called actual match scores. Reason sources are 52 `ML_RF`, 14 `ML_HN_I`, 6 `ML_HN`, 1 `ML_STRAT_F`; fault sources are 50 `RULE`, 23 `WBL_Y`. Temporal matching, not row-number matching, is required because the coarse table has 75 intervals.

#### Player points

Schema: `frame_no` integer; `player_1_x,player_1_y,player_1_conf,player_2_x,player_2_y,player_2_conf` floating point or empty. Pixel X increases right and Y increases down in the expected image canvas; verify source dimensions before registration. Producer `legacy/pipeline/analysis/player_detection.py` exports **bounding-box bottom-center**, not torso center or actual annotated foot joints. It writes whichever first two filtered detections exist in detector order. Slot numbers are neither permanent IDs nor guaranteed near/far assignments.

Slot 1 is present in 29,266 rows; slot 2 in 28,573; both in 28,573. On those paired rows, slot 1 is lower in the image 24,648 times and slot 2 3,925 times. Relative Y order changes on **2,407 adjacent frame pairs**, starting at frames 4, 6, 11 and 12. This confirms the need for anonymous per-frame assignment; it is **not a measured current-pipeline ID-switch count**. No bounding-box extents, human visibility labels, exhaustive negatives, roster bindings or persistent GT IDs are supplied. Any point-matching gate must be declared; unmatched generated points are disagreements, not certified detector FP/FN.

#### Shuttle trajectory

Schema: `Frame` integer; `X,Y` numeric image coordinates; `Visibility` binary; `Confidence` floating point. Zero X/Y consistently accompanies the 4,745 visibility-zero rows; the 24,551 visibility-one rows are all nonzero. The legacy sequence `predict → filter_trajectory → fill_gaps` produces these files. Filled coordinates and visibility share the same schema as observed points, while no interpolation flag is included. `Visibility=1` therefore means retained/generated trajectory availability, not independently verified physical visibility.

At the explicitly diagnostic threshold **Confidence <0.5**, 1,249 visibility-one rows fall below threshold. This is a distribution check only; it neither changes reference visibility nor defines an accuracy denominator. Other historical audits may use other thresholds and must retain their own definitions.

There are **50 rows outside the supplied court JSON's 1280×720 canvas**, at frames **1594–1635** and **16246–16253**. For example frame 1614 is `(551,929)`, and frame 16253 `(721,805)`. Verify the video's actual canvas and coordinate registration first; then inspect these windows visually to distinguish annotation/source scaling mismatch, fill overshoot or other legacy prediction errors. Do not clip or delete them silently, and do not use them as confirmed physical shuttle truth. Preserve these rows in all disagreement denominators with explicit validity categories.

#### Court calibration

`frame_no=300` (candidate 10.0 s at 30 fps); `frame_size={width:1280,height:720}`; `source="manual"`. Corners are ordered **TL(448,305), TR(829,304), BR(933,659), BL(347,659)**. `net_Y=433.5`, `net_top_Y=310.0`; bottom endpoints `(370,435),(908,432)` and cable endpoints `(365,311),(912,309)` retain slight slope. These are image points/lines, not world-metre coordinates. Verify exact source-frame identity, corner interpretation and full-court/singles-court meaning before fitting a homography. A floor homography cannot certify airborne shuttle height, speed, contact, landing or line calls. One manual frame is not a scene-wide calibration truth after cuts.

| Component | Available comparison | Unavailable accuracy claim / required evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Rally segmentation | Coarse-reference overlap with 75 spans; preserved 73-row generated timing reference separately | Generated frame boundaries do not certify physical frame-exact accuracy |
| Player detection | Anonymous bottom-center distance/presence disagreement, source-bound overlays | AP/mAP/box IoU need independent reviewed boxes and exhaustive coverage |
| Tracking and identity | Current track continuity and slot-order diagnostics | IDF1/HOTA/ID switches/fragmentation accuracy need reviewed persistent person IDs and visibility |
| Pose/movement | Execution coverage and source overlays | PCK/OKS, joint/movement accuracy lack independent keypoints or movement labels |
| Shuttle | Availability/localization/trajectory disagreement to generated filled values; separate invalid-canvas rows | Physical precision/recall/localization error require independently reviewed observed coordinates/visibility |
| Racket/contact | Candidate coverage and source-bound frame/event failure review | Precision/recall/F1/temporal error lack exhaustive reviewed contact/racket truth |
| Stroke | Label/unknown distributions; cautiously map rally-level semantics only with explicit role | Per-contact class metrics/confusion cannot use one rally-level `ball_types` value as every contact label |
| Winner/reason | Conditional agreement to primary labels after interval and A/B adjudication, plus abstention/end-to-end coverage | Generated `win_predictions` is never GT; unresolved A/B mapping prevents verified named-winner accuracy |

Use **unavailable/null with the reason**, never a fabricated zero. Separate stage-conditional denominators from full-pipeline coverage and abstention. Keep matching methods, thresholds, source/proxy clocks, model/version/configuration and runtime resource evidence in the run manifest. Reuse earlier rally benchmarks without overwriting or treating this new run as an unchanged historical result. This inventory is the evaluation contract, not a declaration that inference or all requested component accuracy metrics have completed.

as racket observations on Test2. The same head alias recurs in preserved Test1
outputs. This is a verified component evidence weakness; the inspected examples
do not provide a physical precision/recall denominator or establish that each
downstream contact/rally was wrong.

No production source, model, threshold, baseline, original video or annotation
was changed by this investigation. All probes run the CPU image detector with
frozen existing poses. They are neither neural inference nor a new full pipeline
evaluation.

### Why the current gates admit them

Source: `sports/badminton/src/bai_badminton/perception/racket.py`, method
`opencv_ellipse_shaft_v1`.

1. Fresh person detection and same-frame pose are present. This is not a stale
   source-frame or missing-detector explanation for these examples.
2. A wrist-centered search extends0.75 body heights. Heads, clothing, advertising
   and real rackets all fall inside plausible search windows.
3. Accepted diameters span0.07–0.5 body heights with aspect ratio≥0.35. These
   geometric ranges also admit heads and lettering.
4. Median radial fit error≤0.16 and angular coverage≥0.75 measure ellipse-like
   contours, not racket semantics. The selected near head has fit error0.03837,
   coverage1.0, center-to-nose distance1.3895px and wrist distance77.2378px.
5. The shaft test samples24 positions over the interior15–90% of the rim-to-wrist
   gap. It accepts≥65% occupancy after5×5 edge dilation. It does not require a
   connected or consistently oriented shaft reaching both rim and hand.
6. Proposals rank by geometric support, without distinguishing equipment from
   anatomy/background. A better-fitting head can displace a real racket.

| Selected candidate | Dilated shaft occupancy | Exact sampled-edge occupancy |
|---|---:|---:|
| Test2/300/track0 head | 0.8750 | 0.1250 |
| Test2/300/track1 logo | 1.0000 | 0.2917 |
| Test2/1594/track4 torso/wrist | 1.0000 | 0.2083 |
| Test2/1594/track5 lettering | 1.0000 | 0.2917 |

Exact edge occupancy alone is not a replacement gate: a real thin shaft's edges
can sit beside its centerline. The contrast demonstrates that the existing
dilated occupancy does not certify a connected shaft.

The support formula is `0.5 + 0.25*(1-fit_error/0.16) + 0.25*shaft`.
It is an uncalibrated geometric score, not an equipment correctness probability.

### Downstream risk and limits

`events/contact.py::_player_point` substitutes a racket center for the posed
wrists whenever a racket object exists. The contact scorer also uses
`RacketObservation.overlap` and describes equipment overlap as more specific
than another athlete's wrist/body proximity.

`events/contact_evidence.py` can treat fresh racket overlap≥0.5 as an impact cue.
It still applies trajectory, association, current-person and temporal gates;
these examples do not prove a false accepted impact or official point. They
show that a geometric alias can move the proximity anchor or supply misleading
equipment support. The frame-by-frame effect must be measured against the
preserved complete baseline before any pipeline improvement is claimed.

### Diagnostic contract experiments

[Study](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/evaluation/ground_truth_validation/test_02/diagnostics/racket_false_positive_review/contract_study_v3/contract_study.json) contains both Test2 frames,
Test1 frames243/300/9000, and19 synthetic controls. Exact source/helper/cache
hashes are recorded. The controls exercise rotation, scale, blur, partial shaft
occlusion, clean overhead positioning, face overlap, another person's face, and
unconnected transverse clutter. They are engineering controls, not sporting GT.

**Anatomical alias:** an ellipse enclosing at least three confident facial
landmarks identifies positive evidence that the candidate may depict a head.
The prototype checks all fresh detected people's faces, including another
participant in doubles. It does not exclude a player box or a fixed head area.
Clean overhead/near-head rackets outside the facial landmarks remain available.
If a real racket overlaps the face, the correct interpretation is ambiguous
equipment/anatomy, not a claim that the object is definitely a head.

This catches the recurring selected head aliases, but does **not** solve the
detector. Test2/300 has seven accepted candidates: removing the best head still
leaves jersey/body contours. The far logo and lettering remain separate errors.

**Straight shaft evidence:** exploratory Hough-line diagnostics measure straight
edge support in a rim-to-wrist corridor across several angle/corridor widths.
The original fixed2.5px corridor finds no straight support for the four selected
Test2 candidates, while clean scale1 controls retain strong support. It also
rejects unconnected transverse clutter admitted by the current dilation test.
However, that fixed corridor loses scale2 shaft edges; body-relative widths
recover them but can also admit clutter. Short shaft occlusion lowers support.
No threshold in this sensitivity study is validated for production adoption.

The head/arm and real-racket-over-face synthetic examples intentionally contain
the same pixels and posed face. A purely geometric single-frame method cannot
know which physical interpretation is true. Anatomy abstention and straight-line
support are complementary diagnostics, not complete object recognition.

### Proposed acceptance contract and priorities

1. **Preserve candidate provenance and ambiguity.** Generic contour/shaft fits
   remain racket candidates with geometric support. Anatomical-alias or
   unresolved object evidence must not silently become verified equipment or a
   uniquely specific impact cue. Preserve unknown and rejection reasons.
2. **Add a narrow, auditable anatomical-alias abstention** if root authorizes it:
   require multiple confident facial landmarks inside the fitted ellipse,
   respect current pose/person source stamps, and check all target participants.
   Retain the candidate for review rather than declaring a physical negative.
3. **Strengthen independent shaft/object evidence before promotion.** Study
   connected, directional image support with scale/blur/occlusion controls and
   temporal ownership. A straight contour alone can still depict an arm or
   banner. Do not choose a cutoff from these isolated examples.
4. **Evaluate a trained racket detector/temporal association alternative** using
   independently reviewed equipment boxes/centers and ownership/contact labels.
   See the separate alternative-model review; no missing model is claimed loaded.
5. **Measure pipeline effects:** preserve this full baseline; add negative/positive
   contract regressions; rerun affected Test2 and retained Test1 before comparing
   contacts, abstention, segmentation, identity and outcome coverage. A decrease
   in racket observations is not automatically an accuracy improvement.

Risks: facial pose errors may falsely create ambiguity; true racket/face overlap
will lose an equipment cue; small/blurred/edge-on shafts may not support a line;
remaining body/logo candidates can survive. Abstention can reduce false evidence
while increasing unknown coverage. Report both explicitly.

### Validation and provenance

`test_candidate_contract_probes.py`: **12 passed**, covering clean/rotated racket
positives, near-head preservation, explicit face overlap, low-confidence face
landmarks, another participant's face, current-person evidence, transverse hard
negative clutter and straight/blurred shaft positives.

The initial studyv1 hit an OpenCV line-array shape mismatch and was retained;
studyv2 normalized Hough output; studyv3 added scale sensitivity and Test1
controls. Probev1's selected marker initially also marked a duplicate same-center
other-wrist proposal; probev2 requires exact wrist plus center. These were
diagnostic-tool corrections only. Earlier probe outputs remain preserved.

Production `racket.py`, `events/contact.py`, annotations and completed Test1
records remain unchanged by this investigation. This report proposes work;
it does not report a shipped pipeline fix or a physical metric gain.

## Test 2 player-point outliers: source-bound diagnosis

This is an agent qualitative review of **six selected source/proxy frames**, not independently adjudicated player boxes/IDs, AP/mAP or physical localization accuracy. No pipeline fix, inference, matching cutoff or annotation edit was performed. The fresh baseline remains unchanged.

### What the aggregate hides

### Confirmed observations

#### 1. Frame6492: detector-fresh background person, not a target athlete

Both [source overlay](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/evaluation/ground_truth_validation/test_02/diagnostics/player_outlier_review/frame_06492/source_overlay.png) and [actual proxy overlay](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/evaluation/ground_truth_validation/test_02/diagnostics/player_outlier_review/frame_06492/proxy_overlay.png) show the far blue athlete and near red athlete in the normal main court view. Current index0/track8 box **(545.809,233.310)–(636.687,370.534)** follows the far blue athlete; its bottom-center **(591.248,370.534)** agrees with legacy slot2 **(591.192,370.327)** within0.215px.

Current index1/track0 box **(447.318,153.195)–(484.898,206.195)** surrounds the seated dark-clothed **background official above the far baseline**, not either court athlete. It is explicitly `detector_matched=true` and `detector_observed=true`. The real near red athlete is visible around legacy slot1 **(627.424,604.154)** and has no corresponding current person row. This is a confirmed **current target-person population/admission failure** on the inspected source. A generic person detector may correctly detect the official as a person; the analytic error is treating that person as a target player while omitting the visible near athlete.

The minimum-cost anonymous assignment preserves the excellent far match, then necessarily pairs the remaining near-player legacy point with the official's bottom-center **(466.108,206.195)**. That forced pair produces429.411529px. It does not mean one physical athlete's foot was measured429px incorrectly. The final supplied-current population has the wrong semantic member, and the comparator has no independently labelled target-person validity/negative set.

This cache does not preserve every original raw detector proposal at this exact frame. It therefore cannot establish whether the near athlete was missed by the neural detector, lost during tracker association, or excluded by a later selection/filter stage. Trace detector proposals, court admission and tracker links before naming a precise code cause. Do not fix this by fitting a distance cutoff to these rows.

![Background official replaces near athlete](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/evaluation/ground_truth_validation/test_02/diagnostics/player_outlier_review/frame_06492/proxy_overlay.png)

#### 2. Frames6493–6494: propagation retains the bad population

### Population and matching interpretation

The inspected6492–6494/355/25521 rows have two current and two legacy points, so the issue is **wrong semantic population despite equal counts**. Hungarian assignment pairs the smaller population exhaustively without a physical validity gate. Supplementary top-ranked **row-only, not visually inspected here** examples5958,6152,6308 have only one current person, the same track0 near(466,206), versus two legacy points. Their203–230px forced matches and unmatched legacy point counts describe a partial/mismatched population, not reviewed FP/FN or point error for a known athlete. Frame6024 additionally pairs the same official while correctly matching one real near athlete. Preserve these candidates for continuous review; do not silently delete their difficult cases.

No selected source review established that a legacy point is the cause of these largest errors; those legacy points are qualitatively plausible at these instants. That bounded observation does not validate all29,296legacy frames. Pose/keypoint GT, exhaustive target boxes, persistent identities and independent negative labels remain absent. The current matrix must retain its **generated-output disagreement** classification, all unmatched counts and freshness distinctions.

### Next bounded investigation, without blind fixes

1. Trace current detector proposals, matched/unmatched assignments and target-court admission around5958–6497, especially the recurrent small background-official box and the first lost near-athlete observation. Preserve current component thresholds; distinguish person detection from target-player membership.
2. Inspect preceding fresh detections and propagation updates around355 and25521. Determine whether extrapolation, association, cadence/recovery or scene-transition history first diverged; look at complete windows, not only the peak pair distance.
3. Build independently reviewed target-person boxes/visibility and negative examples for these windows plus ordinary controls and doubles/occlusion/adjacent-court cases before AP, recall or tracking-ID accuracy claims. Keep new reviews separate from originals and generated predictions.
4. Evaluate any verified fix as another controlled intervention with before/after Test1/Test2 regressions and fresh perception when person selection changes. The existing engine-only racket-admission experiment does not claim to repair these player tracking/admission failures.

The short-exchange witness gate was recomputed using the exact original contact
evidence consumed by this FSM, rather than later sanitized public contact
payloads. It requires an observed-motion span, disjoint bounded motion windows,
one probable/confirmed trajectory or impact cue, and simultaneous stable opposite
episodes with matching birth/track provenance in both source contexts. Different
track IDs alone do not certify different physical people.

- **G31 andG32:** all tested pair gates pass. Their short intervals are genuinely

  and11802 retrieval. Its long reference tail is not proven continuous airborne

  accepted37-sample interval to fill that tail would merely fit a label.

  trajectory/impact assessments are ambiguous; the required probable cue is
  absent. Source20947/20970 supports a short active sequence, while20994 shows

- **G58:** both21759 and21771 candidates target the same episode despite probable
  trajectory assessments. The opposite-actor gate correctly fails. Reviewed
  source21745/21759/21775/21795 shows relaxed walking/handling. Its canceled
  candidate would geometrically overlap the reference above0.5 if admitted;
  improving that numerical score by accepting walking would be a bad fix.
- **G63:** trajectory can be probable despite insufficient impact; insufficient
  impact alone is not the gate explanation. At23968 the participant pair is
  episodes1/2, but24009 observes1/3 after the far-side track/birth changes. The
  same opposite episode pair cannot be established in both contexts, so the
  typed proof fails. Source23960/23985 supports action, with relaxation/grounded

These controls argue for better perception/episode continuity and reviewed
contact evidence, not globally reducing the60-sample duration threshold. The
existing strong short-proof feature already recovers the cases it can support.

### Ranked improvement and regression priorities

1. **Perception continuity and competing shuttle branches:** G69's−343-frame
   matched end error is the largest observed terminal discrepancy. Review raw
   candidates against source-bound visibility labels; retainG39/G55 and true
   post-point gaps as controls. Improve justified observation/association evidence
   before considering any temporal policy change. Do not substitute low-support
   upper coordinates or airborne floor projections as truth.
2. **Contact/equipment semantics and admission:** verify whether a purported
   racket observation is physical equipment or pose-derived geometry before
   allowing it to substantiate a contact. Test source11353 preparation, true
   short exchangesG31/G32, walkingG58 and post-point pickup. Root owns the
   current candidate and its before/after/regression evidence.
3. **Scene acquisition beyond existing raw candidates:**11346 remains visible
   but unacquired. Develop an independently supported cue with continuous lunge
   controls7703, walking23639, true edit22946, occlusion, missing geometry and
   doubles. Lowering the required region count alone is not a supported fix.
4. **Anonymous episode continuity:** G63 demonstrates why track replacement
   cannot be silently equated with a stable athlete. Improve current observation
   and episode linking with explicit uncertainty; retain the same-actorG58
   control and birth/epoch restrictions.
5. **Reference adjudication:** independently label serve/contact/terminal frames,
   activity versus retrieval, omitted points and cross-edit completeness. Resolve
   named-player/score-row conventions separately. Better labels are necessary
   to rank physical accuracy improvements beyond agreement with legacy proposals.

The Test 1 recovery-frontier, source-score-vote and foot-projection repairs stay
in place. No new temporal defect requiring a blind threshold patch was proven
by this review. Existing policy/source tests and source-derived regression cases
remain useful, but passing them does not establish physical contact, identity,
stroke or winner accuracy. No production code or original data was changed.

## OCR acquisition: demonstrated crop hazard and bounded causal limits

Production code and the active baseline are unchanged. This review separates a
generic engineering defect from an unproven explanation for Test 2's actual
missing readings. Original annotations are not inputs to either probe.

### Generic contract reproduction

`test_roi_expansion_contract.py` records **one failing case and two passing
controls** on current source. The deterministic OCR stub returns only fields
inside its supplied crop. A valid two-row21:19 board first locks a narrow ROI.
The next board retains that completed-game column and adds the current1:0
column to the right, still within the original acquisition corner. The reader
keeps returning21:19, resets its miss counter on each successful parse and never
sees the new column. Full-corner parser input correctly returns1:0. These are
synthetic engineering observations, not manufactured Part2 sporting labels.

The missing guarantee is acquisition completeness: the parser's “rightmost
current column” can only be rightmost among supplied pixels. A valid historical
column inside a permanently cropped ROI is indistinguishable from the current
column without additional context. Existing miss-based unlock cannot recover
when the wrong old column remains parseable. Existing committed spatial-parser
tests cover missing/invalid fields in supplied boxes, but not this ROI growth
and successful-stale-reading loop.

### Real source-pixel demonstration

`probe_real_reader_roi.py` ran the actual unchanged CPU OCR reader with two
explicit threads on the current baseline's proxy. It records actual raw text
boxes, confidences, pixel hashes, crops and ROI overlays under `real_roi_probe/`.
The sparse sequence is deliberately not called a replay of the full worker.

| Actual proxy frame | Retained narrow ROI result | Full top-left acquisition result |
|---|---|---|
|720|AXELSEN0 /ANTONSEN2; initial lock`[274,36,439,92]`|Same0:2|
|8794|16:20|16:20|
|11346|16:21, confidence0.99993|Abstains; raw numeric tokens are`165` and`211`|
|12604|16:21, confidence0.99993|13:2, confidence0.90548; tokens`16 13` and`21 2`|
|22924|16:21, confidence0.99994|Abstains; top current digit is absent from recorded OCR tokens|

The720 standalone reading/confidence matches the first actual cached successful
readout. The8794 narrow reading likewise matches cache. At12604 the source crop
actually contains only the old16:21 game column; the complete corner visibly
contains current13:2 to its right. Thus the acquisition hazard is demonstrated
on real pixels in addition to a synthetic contract.

**This sparse path is not proof of the full worker's ROI history.** The actual
cached reader continues16:20 through9484, then has no reading until12604, where
it returns the current13:2. Therefore the sparse probe's retained stale16:21
cannot be attributed to the active worker without replaying the missing source
calls and view eligibility. The first compact exploratory scan printed only
value changes; the corrected actual missing-read interval is after9484 through
before12604, not after8794. This distinction is preserved explicitly.

At11346 complete pixels still do not solve recognition: the OCR merges adjacent
game fields into three-digit tokens`165` and`211`. Those cannot be silently split
into sporting scores without a verified column/game layout; alternative partitions
exist. The current parser appropriately abstains. Full-corner22924 similarly
does not invent the missing top current digit or attach scores to branding.

### Isolated candidate and tradeoffs

`full_corner_candidate.py` preserves the original successful acquisition corner
instead of narrowing permanently to the detected board bounds. It retains the
existing read cadence, one OCR call per eligible frame, four-corner discovery and
max-miss unlock count. It introduces no numeric threshold, model change, logo
blacklist, video identity or frame exception. This class is not registered or
installed in production.

Three deterministic candidate controls pass: expanded current column is retained
with no extra call, unchanged board remains readable, and exactly the existing
miss budget unlocks and resumes corner search. This addresses the generic
synthetic hazard, without establishing full-video accuracy or an acceptable
performance tradeoff.

The real successful initial board's crop grows from165x56 to576x180 pixels,
approximately11.2times the area. Larger crops can increase OCR runtime, add
unrelated text and create more parser abstention. Full-corner acquisition alone
does not fix fused numeric tokens. A narrower untruncated horizontal-context
policy would be a separate experiment requiring its own positive/negative
controls; no such policy was adopted or silently substituted.

`replay_scheduled_ocr_gap.py` compares current and full-corner readers on every
actual cached main-camera-eligible source frame after9484 through12634, seeded
from successful720/8794/9484 observations. It records every call, ROI/miss/corner
state, readouts and call timing. The result belongs to
`scheduled_gap_replay/report.json` when complete. CPU weights are shared, current
arm runs first, and the GPU baseline shares the host: timings describe this
diagnostic workload, not a controlled production speed benchmark. Intermediate
pre9484 ROI state was not directly logged by the worker and remains a seed-state
limitation even if the later replay matches its cached output.

Do not deploy this candidate merely because its synthetic regression passes.
Use the completed replay, current baseline/all-reference findings and measured
resource tradeoff to decide whether a separate fix is justified. No current
Test 2 score/outcome gain or Test 1 preservation is claimed from these probes.

### Completed scheduled replay: ROI retention is not this gap's cause

The bounded actual-pixel replay is complete. It processes **105 eligible calls**
after9484 through12634 in each arm. Current-source output reproduces the actual
cached reading frames and rows exactly: only12604 and12634 return13:2; there are
no missing/extra readout frames or row mismatches. At12604 confidence0.90548 and
at12634 confidence0.99991 also match the observed current run.

The current reader fails9514,9544,9574 and9604, then **unlocks at9604**. It rotates
the four full acquisition corners and fails to produce a board until12604, where
it locks the now-wider`[274,34,474,95]` ROI. Thus it is not stuck indefinitely on
the initial narrow ROI in this actual gap. The successful seed state and later
output sequence are observationally consistent with the worker, while the
unrecorded intermediate pre9484 state remains an explicit reconstruction limit.

The full-corner candidate follows the same105 calls, unlocks at9604 and returns
the same two13:2 readings at12604/12634. It produces **no additional source
readouts and no measured gap-coverage improvement**. Its12634 confidence differs
(0.91399) because it uses the full corner rather than the successful smaller crop;
neither confidence is calibrated score accuracy.

| Bounded diagnostic measurement | Current reader | Full-corner candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
|Eligible OCR calls|105|105|
|Returned readings|2|2|
|First successful frame after gap|12604|12604|
|Wrong/extra/missing cached row comparisons|0|0|
|Sum of instrumented call time|238.466s|236.087s|

These sums include mostly identical unlocked-corner work, current-first order,
warm shared recognizer state and concurrent host activity. The small difference
does not establish a production speedup or estimate the extra cost of keeping
every successful board at full-corner size.

**Disposition:** retain the generic ROI-expansion hazard and its RED engineering
contract as a future issue, but do not promote the candidate as a Test 2 fix.
The observed Test 2 gap is not explained by persistent narrow-ROI lock. Actual
full-corner11346 shows one concrete token-fusion/parsing limitation; the entire
gap must not be assigned to that single sampled cause. Better acquisition/token
layout research needs source-bound examples and ambiguity controls rather than
invented score partitions. Production remains unchanged.

### Actual22924 positive countercontrol: reject candidate promotion

When the new prefix reached22924, its actual cache recorded `AXELSEN9 /
ANTONSEN12` with confidence0.96547, matching the selected source image. The
standalone full-corner call on that same proxy frame abstains because the upper
current digit was not recognized. Actual current ROI acquisition therefore has
a positive recognition result that the proposed full-corner-only path loses.
The generic stale-ROI synthetic contract does not outweigh this observed
countercontrol and the zero benefit in scheduled gap replay. **Reject adopting
the isolated alternative for Test 2.**

The later actual9:14 read at22954 was independently checked against original
source22945/22946/22954. The display jumps9:12→9:14 at the visible edit22946,
coincident with an actual cached scene barrier and epoch26→27. It is a legitimate
source-text observation across edited footage; treating it as one observed
scoring increment or inventing missing winners would be unsupported.

| Recorded stage | Recorded reason | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| player_identity | `osnet_ain_x0_25: osnet_ain_x0_25 is not downloaded; run ` + `` `bai models fetch osnet_ain_x0_25` `` | Specific local-artifact lookup failure |
| player_reid | `baseline player_reid provider is unavailable` | Generic component-factory consequence of the preceding loader returning no model |

These are **two reporting layers for the same failed construction**, not evidence of two independent missing implementations. The model-staging receipt lists OSNet as `missing_artifact_or_existing_pin`; there is no player-ReID runtime/backend entry. The expected local `models/cache/osnet_ain_x0_25/osnet_ain_x0_25.pt` is absent. The first and last actual cache segments,0–59 and29280–29295, retain `player_identity={state:disabled,model:null,policy:bytetrack_v1,court_membership:observed_box_continuity_v1,requested_model:osnet_ain_x0_25}`. Tracking still executed; neural appearance association did not.

The current configured model/backend/precision **pass the adapter's explicit compatibility checks**. This run failed at the absent file; it did not reach a CUDA initialization or model-forward test. Do not call the configured Torch-CUDA provider unsupported, or claim that merely placing the file guarantees successful inference.

### Exact code path and format caveat

1. `perception/pipeline.py` constructs the ReID component for initial **unknown/doubles** format, or for an explicit `profile.components["player_reid"]` override on singles. The Test2 cache starts with unknown format and later records inferred singles; this explains why this nominal singles video attempted the optional loader.
2. `_load_reid` accepts the pinned model, FP32 and explicit `torch-cpu`/`torch-cuda`. It calls `registry.path(model,fetch=False)`. `engine/runtime/registry.py::ModelRegistry.path` raises the observed missing-artifact error instead of downloading it.
3. On success, the existing `offline_reid.py::OSNetAppearanceEmbedder` independently verifies the exact checkpoint digest before loading its vendored Torch architecture. It takes current bounded BGR image crops, converts to RGB128×256 and returns finite normalized512-dimensional descriptors. It explicitly makes no named-identity claim.
4. The baseline component factory raises its generic provider-unavailable exception when the loader returns `None`. `players.py` consequently has no `PersistentPlayerAssociator`; it retains ByteTrack episode IDs and observed-box court membership. With ReID available, motion/appearance association can maintain a separate canonical visual namespace. Descriptors stay private; they are not authoritative roster evidence.

**Reporting inconsistency to preserve for later review:** `plugin.py::capabilities` currently changes a nonloaded identity stage to `disabled` with a doubles-only explanation whenever the *current* format is not doubles. That public explanation is narrower than the actual loader/provider contract: the provider advertises singles/doubles/unknown, unknown acquisition attempts loading, and an explicit component override can enable singles. Therefore distinguish the authoritative recorded missing-file reason from this generic public format label. It does not establish that the provider lacks an implementation or that current Test2 named identities would become verified if the label were changed. No reporting code was modified here.

### What enabling OSNet could and could not resolve

It could provide a new appearance cue for short-lived track association after occlusion, crossing or raw tracker-ID changes. Crop/model/device failures still have explicit degradation, and the associator retains ambiguity rather than forcing a match. This requires a **separate fresh-perception experiment** with new cache identity and before/after validation; it cannot be silently injected into the current engine-only racket fix or called an unchanged baseline.

It would **not** supply reviewed roster names, PlayerA/B meaning, scoreboard row binding, side-change/game segmentation, team membership, physical hitter confirmation, or verified rally winners. The engine intentionally starts ambiguous; participant episode IDs never automatically become durable roster IDs. A good embedding cannot identify which symbolic annotation label denotes an athlete without a reviewed mapping. The source panels show actual changes of ends and detection-slot swaps, so fixed near/far or slot-index binding is invalid here.

Retain Test1's already implemented **one vote per independent score transition** fix. Repeating OCR/reconciliation calls must not manufacture identity corroboration. Test1's correct source scoreboard acquisition and unknown names were not repaired by falsifying score observations; that conclusion carries forward without reopening the resolved vote defect.

The completed Test2 live ledger contains **75 rally-end events, all with null winners;819 contact events with zero named contact actors;48 identity-ambiguity events**. These are observed output/abstention counts, **not**0% independently measured winner/identity accuracy. They also do not prove OSNet absence is the sole cause: unknown roster/row/point association and physical contact evidence remain separate prerequisites. Ledger SHA256: `655cafec807fbc0b7c65b79a6e600a47f1d06922630b456ef835fb3c50892000`.

### Checkpoint and licence evidence

The publisher's current [LibreReID-osnet model card](https://huggingface.co/LibreYOLO/LibreReID-osnet) lists `osnet_ain_x0_25.pt` with the same exact pinned digest. It declares **MIT for the converted weights**, identifies unchanged conversion from Torchreid multi-source checkpoints, and names **MSMT17, DukeMTMC-reID and CUHK03** as training datasets with research-oriented terms. This is a publisher declaration, not an independent adjudication of all training-data rights. The [current file listing](https://huggingface.co/LibreYOLO/LibreReID-osnet/tree/main) confirms artifact availability; no file was downloaded.

**Code:** upstream [Torchreid licence](https://github.com/KaiyangZhou/deep-person-reid/blob/master/LICENSE) is MIT, with notices to preserve. **Exact checkpoint:** publisher declares MIT and a hash matching the local pin. **Datasets/footage:** their separate terms remain distinct; no blanket permission is inferred from the model/code licence. The local vendored adapter does not require replacing the whole tracker with the model host's external DeepOCSORT stack.

### Evaluation/regression prerequisites

- Keep this one-variable racket-admission experiment's perceptions, model cache/lock, profile and immutable source outputs unchanged. Any subsequent ReID arm needs a separate authorized artifact acquisition/pin receipt and fresh inference; do not retcon appearance descriptors into the current caches.
- Reuse existing regression suites for local-only/checksum/device/precision loading, canonical namespace on inference failure, observed-versus-propagated crop selection, actor provenance and initial unbound singles identity: `test_player_reid_configuration.py`, `test_offline_reid_review.py`, `test_player_association*.py`, `test_unbound_initial_singles_identity.py`, `test_identity_review_ledger.py`, `test_score_mapping_vote_provenance.py`. Their existence is not a claim that this documentation task reran them or loaded real OSNet weights.
- Validate real crop/preprocessing/output parity, bounded person batches, FP32 CUDA compatibility and actual latency/VRAM without replacing the managed Pascal environment. For singles, explicitly record initial unknown versus configured singles and any component override. For doubles, include four players, similar uniforms, teammate crossings, occlusion and team/name uncertainty; generic provider capacity does not certify doubles identity accuracy.
- Part2 Test2 supplies only generated, swapping two-point player slots—**no independently reviewed persistent IDs/boxes/visibility**. Therefore IDF1/HOTA/true ID-switch or fragmentation accuracy is unavailable. Build a separate source-bound review set with identities, visibility, cuts, roster/team/score-row mappings and game changes before claiming accuracy improvement. Anonymous continuity, rejected/ambiguous assignments and named-output coverage can be reported now with their actual denominators.

## Test 2 racket/contact alternatives: evidence and adoption prerequisites

Research only, checked **2026-11-11**. No weights, datasets or packages were downloaded; no model/configuration was replaced. This review starts from the actual fresh frame300 head-adjacent ellipse failures and source-bound component panels, not advertised benchmark scores.

### Local evidence first

`models/manifest.yaml` declares the active built-in `racket_geometry_v1` and a **candidate** `racketvision_racketpose` pointing only to `best_PCK_epoch_90.pth`, with `pin-on-first-fetch`. `models/cache/` currently has no RacketVision/HitNet weights. A pose-only manifest entry is insufficient to run a complete racket detector. The declared MIT label does not independently establish checkpoint rights or authenticity.

Existing [model research](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/docs/research/model-and-algorithm-evaluation.md) already identified this missing two-stage adapter and unresolved model-card terms. The retained [contact study](/home/administrator/Desktop/sport-analytics/Sports_Analytics/docs/research/badmintonai-contact-study-20261103.md) examined visibility-gap, serve-onset and wrist-motion ideas. Current `events/contact.py` already uses shuttle velocity change, proximity and wrist motion, so reintroducing the same cues is not a new improvement. Preserve the completed Test1 fixes and Test2 baseline; evaluate only a specific missing capability through the existing replaceable component contracts.

### Evidence-backed candidates

#### 1. RacketVision RTMDet-M plus racket-specific RTMPose-M

The authors release a complete **racket-box detector followed by five racket keypoints**—top, bottom, handle, left and right. Its output can provide object-specific shape/handle evidence beyond an ellipse near a human wrist. It remains racket perception, not a trained physical-contact verifier. The official inference contract returns a variable list of rackets per frame; player ownership and persistence remain separate work. [Official RacketPose implementation](https://github.com/OrcustD/RacketVision/blob/c44af2a08524d3cb54d818f19686f4cdea4d2793/source/RacketPose/README.md).

Both required checkpoints, **`epoch_300.pth`** (detector) and **`best_PCK_epoch_90.pth`** (pose), are currently listed by the author-linked host; the official downloader maps both to RacketPose. The local manifest lists only the latter. Host revision observed: `a3760773233a0988c9605259743fbdd87c59d3a3`. Availability was checked by listing, not download/deserialization. [Author checkpoint mapping](https://github.com/OrcustD/RacketVision/blob/c44af2a08524d3cb54d818f19686f4cdea4d2793/source/download_checkpoints.py), [checkpoint listing](https://huggingface.co/linfeng302/RacketVision-Models/tree/a3760773233a0988c9605259743fbdd87c59d3a3/checkpoints).

**Licences separately:** repository code is **MIT**; MMDetection and MMPose code are **Apache-2.0**. The model host has **no model card or separately listed LICENSE**, so explicit terms for these exact two checkpoints remain unverified. The dataset card declares **MIT**; the paper says footage comes from professional broadcasts on YouTube, which does not establish redistribution/training rights to every underlying video. Preserve these distinctions. [RacketVision code licence](https://github.com/OrcustD/RacketVision/blob/c44af2a08524d3cb54d818f19686f4cdea4d2793/LICENSE), [MMDetection](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection/blob/main/LICENSE), [MMPose](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmpose/blob/main/LICENSE), [model host](https://huggingface.co/linfeng302/RacketVision-Models), [dataset card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/linfeng302/RacketVision), [paper: data collection](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.17045v3#S3.SS1).

**Singles/doubles:** multiple outputs do not establish four-player owner/contact attribution. No doubles-specific owner/contact validation was verified in the inspected release. Benchmark both formats independently, including overlapping rackets, teammates, occlusion and adjacent courts. Practical prerequisites: verify checkpoint grants/digests; reproduce preprocessing and five-point ordering; isolated compatible OpenMMLab/export environment; validate native/export parity and Pascal runtime; map racket handle to a current observed wrist with ambiguous ownership preserved. Do not install its environment over the working baseline.

#### 2. MonoTrack HitNet: learned temporal hit spotting from pose and shuttle motion

The authors' `MLHitDetector` uses a bidirectional recurrent model over pose, shuttle and court features, with no-hit/bottom-player/top-player outputs. It offers a temporal alternative to making a static ellipse the decisive contact cue. The source also supplies an ad-hoc trajectory-extrema/reachability comparator. **Neither directly detects a racket.** [Author hit-detector source](https://github.com/jhwang7628/monotrack/blob/39e9227bd44fa2a579731b1cc97c7f529f391cd6/python/ai-badminton/src/ai_badminton/hit_detector.py).

**Availability:** training notebooks exist, but the inspected pipeline references `hitnet_conv_model_predict_direction-12-6-0.h5` under a developer's absolute local model path. No public released HitNet artifact, authoritative digest or model card was verified in the inspected repository tree/README. Treat it as an implementation/research lead, not an available drop-in pretrained replacement. [Pipeline model reference](https://github.com/jhwang7628/monotrack/blob/39e9227bd44fa2a579731b1cc97c7f529f391cd6/python/ai-badminton/src/ai_badminton/pipeline_clean.py), [author setup/training instructions](https://github.com/jhwang7628/monotrack).

**Licences separately:** root code is **Adobe Research License**, expressly **noncommercial research/teaching only**, including a restriction on developing commercial products. It is **not MIT**. Exact HitNet weight terms and underlying training-video/annotation rights were not independently established. The root licence cannot be assumed to settle third-party MMPose/MMDetection/TrackNet assets. This is not a production-adoption candidate under the verified grant. [Author licence](https://github.com/jhwang7628/monotrack/blob/39e9227bd44fa2a579731b1cc97c7f529f391cd6/LICENSE).

**Singles/doubles:** the released classifier and dynamic-programming postprocessing explicitly model two players and alternating hitters. It cannot attribute four doubles players without a new contract/model/labels. Its bidirectional temporal window and explicit timing offsets require an offline/latency declaration. Practical prerequisites: clarify permitted use and exact weights; reproduce frame/sample alignment; independently label contacts and negatives; compare a temporal spotter in isolation from outcome/scoring. No source was copied into production.

#### 3. A bounded complementary motion-cue ablation, retaining current perceptions

BadmintonAI's author source combines trajectory acceleration/turns, serve onset and wrist-speed candidates. This can inform a specifically measured missing-contact ablation **without importing a new racket model**. It also illustrates why candidate generation, actor attribution and confirmed physical contact must remain separate. Its match-specific offsets, pixel thresholds and interpolation cannot be transferred to Test2 as facts. Existing overlap with our current component means the exact proposed difference must be demonstrated first. [Pinned author hit implementation](https://github.com/jayclim/BadmintonAI/blob/5c356f05cde0ed90c75316c133e0aba495e5232b/src/badminton/hits.py).

**Licences separately:** original algorithm code is **MIT**. There is no separate trained checkpoint for those rule cues. The complete external stack includes Ultralytics code/models under **AGPL-3.0** according to its own explicit licence inventory; adopting that entire stack has different terms from studying its original cue code. CoachAI's repository supplies an MIT software licence, but annotation and BWF/YouTube footage rights still need dataset-specific verification. [Original code licence](https://github.com/jayclim/BadmintonAI/blob/5c356f05cde0ed90c75316c133e0aba495e5232b/LICENSE), [author dependency inventory](https://github.com/jayclim/BadmintonAI/blob/5c356f05cde0ed90c75316c133e0aba495e5232b/LICENSES/README.md), [CoachAI licence](https://github.com/wywyWang/CoachAI-Projects/blob/main/LICENSE).

**Singles/doubles:** the author distinguishes its singles hit chain from a separate doubles tracking/formation surface; its README explicitly says four-slot hit attribution is not built. Do not call its doubles tracking coverage contact accuracy. Our possible ablation must support all current participants and explicit ambiguity, rather than importing two-player alternation. [Author scope declaration](https://github.com/jayclim/BadmintonAI/tree/5c356f05cde0ed90c75316c133e0aba495e5232b#doubles).

### Required comparison before selection

**Part2 Test2 has no independently reviewed racket boxes/keypoints, physical contact times, exhaustive negative windows or hitter identities.** Generated player/shuttle/winner tables and agent visual panels cannot supply those denominators. No alternative has been measured on this source, and no performance improvement is claimed here.

First preserve a source-bound review set containing visible racket positives, occluded/absent cases, head/banner/jersey/line distractors, serve and net exchanges, current wrist/owner ambiguity, cuts and all four players in separate doubles recordings. Record reviewer status, exact frames/PTS and visibility; keep match-disjoint development and regression/holdout sets. Test1/Test2 are exposed development material, not newly blind holdouts.

Then compare one change at a time: racket box/keypoint localization and owner attribution; contact one-to-one precision/recall/F1 at declared frame tolerances; false contacts per minute; conditional versus end-to-end hitter/class coverage; unknown/abstention and downstream rally/score effects. Include full-run cases with no labels where only coverage is reportable. Preserve current perceptions/configuration for cue ablations and separately record model/preprocessing changes for neural candidates. Measure actual CPU/GPU memory, total runtime and processing latency on the existing server; artifact size or upstream leaderboard values do not establish them.

The closest object-specific candidate is **the complete RacketVision detector-plus-pose pair**, subject to unresolved checkpoint terms, integration and independent labels. MonoTrack remains a restricted research reference. Motion cues are a controlled ablation opportunity only where diagnosis identifies a genuinely missing signal. No generic detector upgrade or unverified leaderboard result justifies replacing the current baseline.

| Component initialization including models seconds | 8.922011024784297 |

The fresh worker used physicalGPU1, **NVIDIA GeForce GTX1080Ti**. RFDETR-Small
and RTMPose executed via ONNX CUDA; TrackNetv3 executed via torch-CUDA FP16.
The receipts record no requested-to-actual backend fallback for these models.
Court geometry, scene continuity, association and OCR include CPU work. Thus GPU
use does not make every stage GPU-bound or make wall time pure neural latency.
The worker takes56.37minutes for16.28minutes of source footage, around3.46×
source duration. Pure neural-only throughput and isolated model-loading latency
are explicitly unavailable.

| Measured stage invocation scope | Calls | Accumulated seconds | P50 ms | P95 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| court | 489 | 153.922 | 306.088 | 396.013 |
| content_continuity_and_players | 489 | 1441.222 | 3311.936 | 3617.652 |
| shuttle | 489 | 427.121 | 847.660 | 1099.133 |
| players | 489 | 128.370 | 242.848 | 542.680 |
| ocr | 489 | 451.860 | 936.343 | 1059.779 |

These are saved invocation wall-time scopes; some overlap. They must not be
summed into an invented pure-neural budget or compared as a controlled speedup.
GPU/RSS peaks are sampled and can miss short peaks; tree RSS may count shared
pages more than once. CPU resource competition from unrelated jobs is not
excluded by these receipts. Decode/perception/cache runner scope is2790.788s.

There is a **redundant reporting-field limitation**:
`bound_reference_diagnostics/component_reference_metrics.json.executed_models`
is null because that summary lookup uses `worker_info.loaded_models`, while the
worker receipt exposes `models`. This does not indicate missing or failed
inference. Actual, verified provenance is available in
`run/inference.json.models`, `run/inference.json.execution_backends`,
`analysis/technical_analysis.json.model_sets_from_actual_caches`, and
`analysis/technical_analysis.json.models_verified_during_analysis`.
Model identities and hashes are preserved in the independent JSON review too.
No immutable matrix/helper was edited to change this field during the active run.

RFDETR-Small1.4.2, RTMPose-M body7 and TrackNetv3 checkpoint hashes are verified.
OCR package detector/classifier/recognizer weights are separately hashed.
OSNet and RacketVision are explicitly unavailable, not claimed loaded; no
alternative model performance is invented. The source plan, profiles, applied
fix receipt and environment remain the authoritative implementation/configuration
provenance for the fresh run.

This review establishes actual fresh execution, unchanged raw observations,
reproduced semantic effects and explicit metric limitations. It does not replace
the enclosing final completion receipt, final consolidated matrix, or physical
ground-truth accuracy requirements.
